title: Ezekiel 43:18–27
context: The Lord GOD gives the ordinances for consecrating the altar. The Levitical priests of the offspring of Zadok are to offer a young bull for a sin offering, putting its blood on the altar’s horns, ledge, and border to cleanse it and make atonement for it. On the second day a male goat is offered, then a bull and a ram as burnt offerings with salt. For seven days the altar is purified, and from the eighth day the priests will offer the people’s burnt offerings and peace offerings, and the LORD says, I will accept you. The rite recalls the consecration of the altar in Exodus 29:36-37 and Leviticus 8:15, 33. The mention of sacrifices raises a question readers handle differently. Some who expect a literal future temple see memorial or purifying offerings, while others read the sacrifices as Ezekiel’s picture of restored worship in the terms of his day, fulfilled in Christ’s “one sacrifice for sins forever” (Hebrews 10:12). Both views are held among Arminian and Reformed readers.

verses.text: He said to me, “Son of man, the Lord GOD says: ‘These are the ordinances of the altar in the day when they make it, to offer burnt offerings on it, and to sprinkle blood on it.
verses.arminianNotes: These are the ordinances of the altar in the day when they make it, Arminian readers see the Lord GOD giving instructions for consecrating the altar for burnt offerings and the sprinkling of blood.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that the voice is the Lord GOD speaking to the prophet. Both traditions read the ordinances within the larger vision, whatever view of the temple they hold.

verses.text: You shall give to the Levitical priests who are of the offspring of Zadok, who are near to me, to minister to me,’ says the Lord GOD, ‘a young bull for a sin offering.
verses.arminianNotes: You shall give to the Levitical priests who are of the offspring of Zadok, Arminian readers see the Zadokite priests chosen to minister, as also named in 40:46 and 44:15.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that a young bull for a sin offering recalls Leviticus 4:3. The priests who are near to the LORD minister in his presence, as in the earlier Levitical order.

verses.text: You shall take of its blood and put it on its four horns, and on the four corners of the ledge, and on the border all around. You shall cleanse it and make atonement for it that way.
verses.arminianNotes: You shall take of its blood and put it on its four horns, Arminian readers see the cleansing of the altar through blood on the horns, corners of the ledge, and border all around.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note the similar rite in Leviticus 8:15, where Moses puts blood on the horns of the altar to make atonement for it. The parallels are named without harmonizing them.

verses.text: You shall also take the bull of the sin offering, and it shall be burned in the appointed place of the house, outside of the sanctuary.
verses.arminianNotes: You shall also take the bull of the sin offering, Arminian readers notice the bull burned in the appointed place outside the sanctuary, following the pattern of the sin offering in the law.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers compare Leviticus 4:12, where the bull is burned outside the camp. Some Christian readers also connect such outside burning with Hebrews 13:11-12, a typological reading offered as an option.

verses.text: “On the second day you shall offer a male goat without defect for a sin offering; and they shall cleanse the altar, as they cleansed it with the bull.
verses.arminianNotes: On the second day you shall offer a male goat without defect Arminian readers follow the cleansing continued on the second day, with the altar cleansed as it was with the bull.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note the requirement without defect, which runs through the sacrificial law. The repeated cleansing on successive days emphasizes the thoroughness of the altar’s preparation.

verses.text: When you have finished cleansing it, you shall offer a young bull without defect and a ram out of the flock without defect.
verses.arminianNotes: When you have finished cleansing it, you shall offer a young bull without defect and a ram out of the flock without defect. Arminian readers see the move from cleansing to burnt offering.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that the sin offerings precede the burnt offerings, following the order of the law. Purification comes before dedication, a pattern both traditions observe.

verses.text: You shall bring them near to the LORD, and the priests shall cast salt on them, and they shall offer them up for a burnt offering to the LORD.
verses.arminianNotes: You shall bring them near to the LORD, and the priests shall cast salt on them, Arminian readers see salt used in the offering, recalling the salt of the covenant in Leviticus 2:13.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that the burnt offerings are offered up to the LORD. The use of salt connects this rite with the covenant ordinances of the law.

verses.text: “Seven days you shall prepare every day a goat for a sin offering. They shall also prepare a young bull and a ram out of the flock, without defect.
verses.arminianNotes: Seven days you shall prepare every day a goat for a sin offering. Arminian readers take the seven-day pattern as a sign of completeness in the altar’s consecration.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers compare Exodus 29:37, where atonement is made for the altar for seven days. The young bull and the ram are also prepared daily, without defect.

verses.text: Seven days shall they make atonement for the altar and purify it. So shall they consecrate it.
verses.arminianNotes: Seven days shall they make atonement for the altar and purify it. Arminian readers see the consecration completed, the altar made ready for its proper use in worship.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note the phrase so shall they consecrate it. They read the atonement here as cleansing the altar, while Christian readers of both traditions confess Christ’s once-for-all offering (Hebrews 10:12).

verses.text: When they have accomplished the days, it shall be that on the eighth day and onward, the priests shall make your burnt offerings on the altar and your peace offerings. Then I will accept you,’ says the Lord GOD.”
verses.arminianNotes: When they have accomplished the days, Arminian readers see the eighth day as the beginning of regular worship, when the priests make your burnt offerings and your peace offerings on the altar.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers hear Then I will accept you as shared ground on God’s gracious acceptance of his people. See the Hebrews 10:14 box on Christ’s single offering, by which he has perfected forever those who are being sanctified.
